title: How much does model-predictive heating and cooling save over a thermostat on a time-of-use tariff, when the model and forecast are wrong?
lede: Does MPC beat a thermostat for a heat pump on a time-of-use tariff? On real TMY3 weather with a deliberately wrong model and yesterday's weather as the forecast it pays 10.7% less in Greensboro (4.1% in cold Sand Point), saves more with more thermal mass (6.5% to 25%), and loses the gain at an 8 K forecast error; the envelope is from published values, not a fit to measured data.
summary: A two-state RC house (ASHRAE 140 Case 600 style envelope, recalled and not checked) with a heat pump (Staffell et al. 2012 COP fit) on NREL TMY3 hourly weather for Greensboro NC and Sand Point AK, a PI thermostat, and a receding-horizon LP controller (HiGHS, 24 h) on an assumed three-band tariff. The controller's model is wrong by a stated amount (true loss +15 to 30%, lighter, sunnier) and its forecast is yesterday's weather. Greensboro: $783 a year against $877 for a 20/24 thermostat (−10.7%), with 2,383 against 7,621 K h outside the 20–24 °C band; a thermostat tuned to 2,839 K h pays $1,300. Flat tariff 4.8%; Sand Point 4.1% and 2.4%. The saving grows with peak/off-peak ratio (4.9% to 14.7%) and thermal mass (6.5% to 25%), and vanishes at 8 K forecast error. Not sourced: heat capacities (swept), cooling COP, solar factor, tariff and 6 kW capacity (assumed); no measured building data was reachable, so nothing is fitted. Simulation only.
